title: Build a Slack Help Desk That Files Tickets in Google Sheets
summary: Build a Slack help desk that logs approved hardware tickets in Google Sheets. Follow a 0:18 audio dropout from the first message to the engineer’s row.
body_markdown:
“The speakerphone went silent during our test clip.” When that message lands in Slack, the person who heard the dropout still has the cable in hand. Ask them to change one thing before they leave the room, and the engineer who gets the ticket has something to try.


You’ll build a **Slack help desk that files support tickets in Google Sheets** . We ran this one with a fictional speakerphone called **Pebble Dock** . The clip went silent at **0:18** with the original USB cable and again at **0:18** with its replacement. Here’s what the reporter approved in Slack and what the engineer received in Sheets.


Slack preserves the reporter’s “Yes, file that report.” In cell D2 of the new row, the engineer gets the full retest, including what stayed the same.


You’ll need a Slack workspace where you can install an app, a Google account that can create a spreadsheet, and a Quickchat AI account with credits for replies. For a company desk, choose a plan with commercial use. The downloadable kit contains the guide, prompt, tab headers, Action settings and test messages.[Get the Pebble Dock practice kit](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/pebble-dock-slack-triage.zip) ·[Plans and limits](https://quickchat.ai/docs/pricing-and-plans) .


If your desk is already configured,try the Slack conversation .


## 1. Where should Slack support tickets land in Google Sheets?


Give the engineer one tab called **Triage** , with the original symptom and the retest in adjacent columns. “Tried another cable” describes an action. The next person also needs to know what happened when the clip played again.


1. Sign in to Quickchat AI. Use the empty Agent in a new account. If you already have a working Agent, choose **Add new AI Agent** from the switcher. Choose **Set up manually** and name the practice Agent **Pebble Dock desk** under **Identity** .[Create a Quickchat AI account](https://app.quickchat.ai/register) .
2. Open **Actions & MCPs → Add Action → Google Sheets → Connect Google Sheets** . Approve the connection in the Google account that will own the queue. The connection creates a spreadsheet called **Quickchat Leads** and enables a starter Action named` log_lead_to_google_sheet` . Switch that Action off in **Actions & MCPs** and keep it for its spreadsheet ID. Choose **Open sheet** in the Google Sheets connection to open the file.[Google Sheets connection walkthrough](https://quickchat.ai/post/connect-ai-agent-to-google-sheets) .


Choose the Google account that should own the ticket queue. Open sheet takes you back to the file created in that account.


1. In the spreadsheet, add a tab next to **Leads** and name it **Triage** . Open` triage-headers.tsv` from the kit in a text editor, copy its one line and paste into **A1** . You should see **model** , **mode** , **observation** , **retest** and **conversation** across A1:E1. Freeze the header row and wrap columns C and D so the two runs are easy to compare.


On the Triage tab, row 1 names the five fields and row 2 is empty. The close-ups show the exact tab and headers used for this desk.


1. If you’re handing tickets to a colleague, use **Share** to give them **Viewer** access to the file. To follow the conversation link in column E, they’ll also need an available seat and **Support** access or higher on this Agent. For a solo run, open both as the owner.[Quickchat AI team roles](https://quickchat.ai/docs/team-and-roles) .


## 2. What should the Slack help desk ask about the speakerphone?


“Try another cable” would be a strange first reply to someone using Bluetooth. Give the desk one question that decides which part of the guide to open. A USB reporter checks a second cable. A Bluetooth reporter checks which output the laptop selected.


1. Before adding the internal guide, open **Your Website → Install → Availability and access** . Turn off **Widget & Embed access** , choose **Nobody** for **Chat Page Access** , and set **AI assistants** on the Install page to **Visitors only** . Leave unused channels disconnected.[Website access settings](https://quickchat.ai/docs/channels/ai-assistant-access) .
2. In **Knowledge Base → Add Article** , name the article **Pebble Dock desk guide** . Paste the guide below, save it and wait for **Ready** . For a different device, use its own support procedure.[Knowledge Base](https://quickchat.ai/docs/ai-agent/knowledge-base) .


Copy the Pebble Dock desk guide


```text
Pebble Dock is the speakerphone in this demo. Check the device label and ask whether the reporter used USB or Bluetooth.


USB: When the sound drops, ask whether the laptop still lists Pebble Dock as the selected audio output. Keep the same laptop, port, volume and test clip. Swap in a second known-good USB cable and replay the clip once. Record what changed and when the sound stopped on each run.


Bluetooth: Ask which playback device was selected when the sound dropped. Select Pebble Dock and play the same clip once. Record whether the sound returns and the selected output before and after the retest.


If playback returns, summarize the observation and finish. For a persistent fault, let the reporter check the four report fields and decide whether to file. If the device label is unfamiliar, ask the room's support contact for its guide. The engineer investigates the cause.
```


See the guide in the Knowledge Base editor


The Ready article gives the desk two checks. A reporter who used Bluetooth gets the playback-device comparison.


1. In **Identity → AI Persona → Main Prompt → Edit** , paste the Main Prompt below and save. It tells the desk to keep the two observations separate, read them back and ask the reporter whether to file.


Copy the Main Prompt


```text
Use the Pebble Dock desk guide. Establish the model and connection mode, then ask one question at a time. Offer only the relevant comparison from the guide. Record what happened before the comparison separately from what happened on the retest. Keep the reporter’s timing and selected output if given. Never guess a cause.


If playback returns, summarize the result and finish. If the drop persists, read back the model, mode, original observation and retest. Ask whether to file that exact report. Only call Log reproducible report after the reporter confirms. A withdrawal ends the request. A successful append in this conversation covers the report; repeated confirmation does not start another. Acknowledge success only when the Action returns a successful write. If the outcome is uncertain, ask the desk to inspect Triage before trying again.
```


You can see which instructions the Agent actually used. After our reporter answered “USB,” we opened that reply in **Inbox → Why AI said that** . The source points straight to the paragraph about keeping the laptop, port, volume and clip the same.


A search for “Pebble Dock USB playback drop comparison” led the Agent to this passage in the desk guide.


## 3. How does an approved report become a Google Sheets row?


The reporter supplies four things. Quickchat AI already knows the fifth, the address of this conversation. Give the Agent one **API Action** that writes all five to a single row after the reporter approves.


1. Go to **Actions & MCPs → Add Action → API Action → Create manually** . Name it **Log reproducible report** , choose **AI decides** under **When to run** , and paste this **API Action Description** .


```text
Use only after the reporter reviews and explicitly confirms the model, connection mode, original observation and retest for a persistent Pebble Dock problem. Submit one report for this conversation. If the retest fixed playback, the reporter withdraws, or a row was already saved, finish without filing.
```


1. Under **What to ask the user first** , add these four **Text** parameters. Mark each **Required** and choose **No default** .


Parameter Description to enter


` model` Device label confirmed by the reporter.


` mode` Connection used for the test: USB or Bluetooth.


` observation` Original playback behavior, including timing and selected output when supplied.


` retest` What the reporter changed, the conditions they kept, and what they heard on the repeat.


1. In **API Endpoint** , choose **POST** . Copy the URL from the disabled lead Action. Keep its real spreadsheet ID and replace everything after` /values/` with` Triage!A:E:append?valueInputOption=RAW` . In the example,` FILE_ID` stands for the ID already in that URL.


Copy the endpoint format


```text
https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/FILE_ID/values/Triage!A:E:append?valueInputOption=RAW
```


In **Headers** , enter these two name/value pairs. Keep the token placeholder as written. Quickchat AI supplies the credential when the request runs.


Header Value


` Authorization`` Bearer {{google_sheets_access_token}}`


` Content-Type`` application/json`


In **API Endpoint → Body** , turn on **JSON** and paste the block below. Its inner array fills one row from A to E.` RAW` keeps a report beginning with an equals sign as literal text.[Google Sheets append reference](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets.values/append) .


Copy the JSON for the Body tab


```text
{
"values"  : [
[  "{{model}}"  ,   "{{mode}}"  ,   "{{observation}}"  ,   "{{retest}}"  ,   "{{conversation_url}}"  ]
]
}
```


Check the five cells in the Action editor


The last value is the Inbox address supplied by Quickchat AI. The other four come from the report.


1. Under **Save to memory → Add value** , choose **API response** as the **Source** . Enter` $.updates.updatedRange` in **Value to save** and` triage_row` in **Memory key** . When Google appends a row, it returns the cells it wrote, such as` Triage!A2:E2` on a fresh tab.
2. Under **Run only when → Add condition** , enter` triage_row` and select **does not exist** . Save the changes and **Enable** the Action. After the range is stored, another “yes” in that conversation will be blocked from sending the row again.[Run conditions](https://quickchat.ai/docs/ai-agent/actions#run-only-when) ·[Saving a response value](https://quickchat.ai/docs/ai-agent/actions#save-to-memory) .


Use the same memory key in both fields. A successful write fills it with the range in Sheets.


## 4. How do you file a hardware ticket in one Slack thread?


Now try the desk from the reporter’s side. Leave **Triage** open in another tab and note the last occupied row.


1. In Quickchat AI, open **External Apps → Slack → Connect to Slack** . Select your test workspace and review the permissions. Slack displays a review notice for apps outside its Marketplace. If your workspace requires approval, send the install request to your app manager.[Installing apps in Slack](https://slack.com/help/articles/202035138-Add-apps-to-your-Slack-workspace) .
2. Back in Quickchat AI, check that **Enable Slack** is on. Leave **Reply to all messages in channel** and **Reply to everyone in thread** off. The desk will answer a channel mention and continue with the person who started the thread.[Slack connection settings](https://quickchat.ai/docs/channels/slack) ·[Slack chatbot setup walkthrough](https://quickchat.ai/post/how-to-build-a-gpt-3-ai-slack-chat-bot) .
3. Open a test channel. In its header, choose **Agents & apps** and add **Quickchat AI** . If the channel already has apps, choose **Add more** . We used` #hardware-triage` .[Adding an app to a Slack channel](https://slack.com/help/articles/33076000248851-Work-with-AI-agents-in-Slack) .


Find the two Slack reply switches in Quickchat AI


This is the panel before connection. After authorization, Enable Slack should be on. The two Reply switches stay off for this desk.


The first mention goes in the channel. For the retest, use the thread’s Reply box. Leave Also send to #hardware-triage unchecked to keep follow-ups out of the main channel.


**Start with the label.** Type` @` , select **Quickchat AI** in Slack’s mention picker and send “The device label says Pebble Dock. The speakerphone went silent during our test clip.” Open the reply thread. Our desk asked, **“Was the speakerphone connected by USB or Bluetooth?”**


The mention starts the ticket in the channel. Open its thread to answer the connection question.


**Run the same clip twice.** Reply in the thread with the first observation. “USB. The sound cut at 0:18 and Pebble Dock was still selected on the laptop.” The desk asks for a second known-good USB cable. Use the same laptop, port, volume and test clip. Reply with what you heard. Our reporter wrote, “The sound cut at 0:18 again. Pebble Dock was still selected.”


The reporter kept Pebble Dock selected. When the clip reached 0:18 on the replacement cable, the sound cut again. That second timestamp is what the engineer needs.


**Check the readback before you file.** The desk lists the model, connection, original observation and retest, then asks **“May I file this exact report?”** This is the moment to correct a missing timestamp or a misheard result. When all four fields match, reply **“Yes, file that report.”**


The filing receipt appears in the same Slack thread, directly under the reporter’s approval.


If the replacement cable plays the whole clip, tell the desk that instead. It should summarize the recovery in Slack and leave the engineering queue alone.


## 5. How does the engineer verify the ticket in Google Sheets?


Switch back to **Triage** . Our empty tab now had exactly one report in **` Triage!A2:E2`** . The engineer can read **Pebble Dock** and **USB** in the first two cells, then compare the tests without opening Slack.


Read across row 2. Column C preserves the first dropout and selected output. Column D adds the second cable, the conditions the reporter kept and the same 0:18 result.


**Follow column E back to the conversation.** Open its link while signed in to Quickchat AI, find the final reply in **Inbox** and expand **1 action called** . In our run, **Log reproducible report** returned HTTP **200** . With **Editor access or higher** , you can also open **Actions & MCPs → Log reproducible report → View logs** . Google’s response named the same range,` Triage!A2:E2` , with one row and five cells updated.[Using the Quickchat AI Inbox](https://quickchat.ai/docs/conversations/inbox) .


The link in the fifth cell opens this exchange. Expand the Action on the filing reply to see which request succeeded.


What can the next engineer try? The sound stopped at the same point with both cables, and the dock stayed selected. Replaying the same clip on a different audio output would help distinguish a problem in the clip from one in the playback path. For a real ticket, include the room and clip filename when the reporter knows them. If the reporter asks for a person, you can also[notify the support team in Slack on handoff](https://quickchat.ai/post/slack-notification-ai-action) .


Check a recovered device, a withdrawn report or a second confirmation


In separate local practice runs, restoring playback on USB or Bluetooth ended the conversation with a summary and zero writes. Withdrawing before approval also left the queue untouched. Use a fresh thread for each case in the kit.


The two local runs reached different outcomes. Only the persistent dropout with confirmation sent a request to the test receiver.


To test a repeated confirmation, go back to the original thread and say “Yes, file that same report again.” A saved` triage_row` blocked a second request in our local test. If a write times out, check column E for the conversation link before retrying. The first write may already have reached Google.


Test the first question again after changing your guide


In **Conversations → Testing** , create a dataset. Add “The meeting-room speaker went silent during the test clip” and “My Maple Loop stopped playing” as independent messages. Set the evaluation criterion to “Clarifies the model or connection before giving a device-specific check.” Run the dataset and read the replies. Use the Slack thread and its row to check the full handoff.[Simulation testing](https://quickchat.ai/docs/conversations/testing) .


Prepare the desk with ChatGPT or Claude


Connect your Quickchat AI account in your AI client and attach the unzipped practice files. Give it this request. The workspace owner completes the Slack and Google sign-ins.[Quickchat AI account connection](https://quickchat.ai/docs/manage-with-ai) ·[ChatGPT app](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a4656c688748191be4c5247fb0d5dfc) ·[Claude connector](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/app-quickchat-ai) .


```text
Prepare the Pebble Dock desk Agent using the attached guide and Main Prompt. Draft Log reproducible report using my connected spreadsheet’s ID and the supplied Action settings. Show me the four parameters, the conversation link, the memory mapping and the run condition before enabling it. Leave workspace authorization and the first confirmed test report for me.
```


## Frequently asked questions


### Can I create a support ticket from a Slack thread without writing code?


Yes. In Quickchat AI, connect Slack and Google Sheets, then configure an API Action with the request in this guide. The Agent collects the report in a Slack thread, asks the reporter to approve it and appends one row to Sheets.


### What should a reproducible hardware report include?


Record the device label, the connection, what happened on the first run, and what changed on a repeat of the same test. Include the playback time and selected audio output when the reporter supplies them. A conversation link lets the engineer check the original wording.


### Can I send Slack tickets to an existing Google Sheet?


The Quickchat AI connection creates a spreadsheet called Quickchat Leads in the Google account you authorize. Add the Triage tab there. To use an existing tracker, copy its headers or data into the connected file, or use an integration with permission to write to the existing file.


### Where does the conversation link in Google Sheets open?


Column E opens the original Slack conversation in Quickchat AI Inbox. A teammate needs access to the spreadsheet and Support access or higher on that Agent. In Inbox they can read the messages and inspect the filing Action on the final reply.


### Will confirming the same Slack support ticket twice add two rows to Google Sheets?


After a successful write, Quickchat AI saves the returned range in triage_row. The Action then blocks a second write on a later turn in that conversation. If a request times out, check column E for the conversation link before retrying. Simultaneous requests can still produce duplicates.
